name: Roastmate Original Roast Library

jokes.text: Your pawn wandered off like Peter chasing a cutaway. The plot is still in the center.
Your queen is Stewie with a laser: impressive equipment, questionable supervision.
That piece has a longer recurring bit than Peter fighting the chicken.
Your piece is attacked. Peter’s health insurance would refuse this episode.
You took the center. A Family Guy plot finally survived the cutaway.
A piece developed. Brian will claim he thought of it first.
Their piece disappeared faster than a sensible decision in Quahog.
You castled. Even Lois would approve this one household decision.
Check. Their king just heard Stewie lock the door.
What the fuck was that? Peter Griffin gets a reset next episode. Your king has to live in this mess.
Your pawn went sideways like Riley turning a serious conversation into a music-video audition.
Your queen brought Riley’s swagger. Did she bring Huey’s plan?
That piece is doing a Granddad argument: same point, louder outfit.
Your piece is attacked. Huey warned you; Riley clicked anyway.
Center claimed. Huey finally got control of the remote.
Your piece left home. Granddad wants to know who’s paying for the trip.
You collected a piece. Riley is already exaggerating the story.
You castled. Granddad got the house insured before the next episode.
Check. The king’s peaceful afternoon just became a Boondocks incident.
Huey drew up the strategy, Riley clicked the mouse, and now Granddad wants his deposit back.
Your pawn is on a side mission. Michael Scott calls it a regional expansion.
Your queen entered like Michael calling a meeting nobody requested.
Same piece again. This opening has become a meeting about the previous meeting.
Your piece is attacked. Dwight’s emergency drill has stopped being theoretical.
Center control. Jim would look straight into the camera and nod.
A piece developed. More productive than an entire Dunder Mifflin meeting.
You captured a piece. Dwight has laminated the incident report.
You castled. Your king has transferred out of Michael’s branch.
Check. Their king is having a Scott’s Tots moment.
Michael Scott signed this strategy. Dwight notarized it. Jim is looking at the camera like the documentary is evidence.
Your pawn went to the edge. The center is not Ross’s couch; you can put it there.
Your queen is doing a solo tour. This is Friends, not The One With Only Rachel.
Same piece again. Apparently you and development are on a break.
Your piece is attacked. Nobody told you life on that square was gonna be this way.
You claimed the center. Finally, somebody can afford this apartment.
A piece developed. Joey has discovered a second career option.
You took their piece. Joey would have refused to share it anyway.
You castled. Your king got an apartment without the drama.
Check. The king’s next move needs more than Ross yelling PIVOT.
Your pieces are like Ross and Rachel: a whole lot of history and nobody can explain the current arrangement.
Your pawn went nowhere near the action. An opening about nothing.
Your queen entered like Kramer: abruptly, uninvited, and near danger.
Same piece again. George has turned one errand into a season.
Your piece is attacked. You picked the chess equivalent of George’s parking space.
Center claimed. Finally, this episode is about something.
A piece developed. George is putting that achievement on his résumé.
You captured a piece. The opponent’s position has a shrinkage problem.
You castled. Your king found a room Kramer cannot burst into.
Check. Their king is suddenly very concerned about the exit policy.
George Costanza would invent a fake job to avoid taking responsibility for that move.

Your queen arrived in Bel-Air with no luggage and too much confidence.
Same piece again. Carlton has one dance and you have one employee.

Center claimed. You finally own more real estate than the cab fare.
A piece developed. Geoffrey would like the rest of the household to help.
Their piece got evicted. Uncle Phil handled the paperwork personally.
You castled. Your king made it to Bel-Air before the trouble caught up.
Check. Their king just saw Uncle Phil standing in the doorway.
This position has Will’s confidence and Carlton’s street survival plan.
Your pawn went to the edge. The center is not asking you to get out.
